http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos#definitio.@value: Defining the external and internal parameters to be taken into account when managing risk, and setting the scope and risk criteria for the risk management policy.

Physical or psychological injury related to a person i.e. service user, staff member or member of the public.

http://www.w3.org/2000/01/rdf-schema#com.@value: A person with responsibility for directly managing individual employees or teams. In turn, they report to a higher level of management on the performance and well-being of the employees or teams they manage.

http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos#definitio.@value: To check, supervise, observe critically or record the progress of an activity, action or system on a regular basis in order to identify change.

http://www.w3.org/2000/01/rdf-schema#com.@value: Project slippage and failure to meet objectives of projects.

http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos#definitio.@value: Project slippage and failure to meet objectives of projects.

http://www.w3.org/2000/01/rdf-schema#com.@value: Operational risks relate to the day-to-day delivery of activities, operational business plans and objectives. Operational risks typically have a short-term focus. Whilst they may impact a number of areas of the service, this does not necessarily make them a strategic risk. Operational risks may have the ability to impact strategic and other operational risks.

http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos#definitio.@value: Operational risks relate to the day-to-day delivery of activities, operational business plans and objectives. Operational risks typically have a short-term focus. Whilst they may impact a number of areas of the service, this does not necessarily make them a strategic risk. Operational risks may have the ability to impact strategic and other operational risks.

http://www.w3.org/2000/01/rdf-schema#com.@value: Project risks relate to the achievement and delivery of the project objectives and outcomes. The majority of project risks are short term in nature and exist for the term of the project, whilst some will be on-going and re-classified at the end of the project. Projects can be defined as temporary, with the aim of delivering outcomes within a specified timeframe.

http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos#definitio.@value: Project risks relate to the achievement and delivery of the project objectives and outcomes. The majority of project risks are short term in nature and exist for the term of the project, whilst some will be on-going and re-classified at the end of the project. Projects can be defined as temporary, with the aim of delivering outcomes within a specified timeframe.

http://www.w3.org/2000/01/rdf-schema#com.@value: The remaining level of risk after all treatment plans have been implemented.

http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos#definitio.@value: The remaining level of risk after all treatment plans have been implemented.

http://www.w3.org/2000/01/rdf-schema#com.@value: Using information from incident management to inform a proactive approach to managing risk. Data relating to incidents which occur is a critical source of information about risk. Incident data can be used both to identify risk and also to monitor the effectiveness of actions taken to prevent its recurrence.

http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos#definitio.@value: Using information from incident management to inform a proactive approach to managing risk. Data relating to incidents which occur is a critical source of information about risk. Incident data can be used both to identify risk and also to monitor the effectiveness of actions taken to prevent its recurrence.

http://www.w3.org/2000/01/rdf-schema#com.@value: Informed decision to take a particular risk.

http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos#definitio.@value: Informed decision to take a particular risk.

http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos#definitio.@value: Overall process of risk identification, risk analysis and risk evaluation.

http://www.w3.org/2000/01/rdf-schema#com.@value: Informed decision not to be involved in, or to withdraw from, an activity in order not to be exposed to a particular risk. Risk avoidance may increase the significance of other risks or may lead to the loss of opportunities for gain.

http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos#definitio.@value: Informed decision not to be involved in, or to withdraw from, an activity in order not to be exposed to a particular risk. Risk avoidance may increase the significance of other risks or may lead to the loss of opportunities for gain.

http://www.w3.org/2000/01/rdf-schema#com.@value: The categories used by the organisation to group similar opportunities or risks for the purposes of reporting and assigning responsibility.

http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos#definitio.@value: The categories used by the organisation to group similar opportunities or risks for the purposes of reporting and assigning responsibility.

http://www.w3.org/2000/01/rdf-schema#com.@value: Terms of reference against which the significance of a risk is evaluated.

http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos#definitio.@value: Terms of reference against which the significance of a risk is evaluated.

http://www.w3.org/2000/01/rdf-schema#com.@value: In instances where a risk was notified to and accepted onto the register of a more Senior Manager for oversight it may be that following the implementation of actions the rating of the risk may have reduced to an acceptable or tolerable level or where remaining actions lie within the control of the Manager at the level below. In such circumstances a decision may be taken to ‘close’ the risk on the register and to de-escalate it onto the register of the Manager on the level below. Such risks when added to the register below are given a risk status of ‘open’ on that register and are reviewed at the next Management Team meeting of that Manager.

http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos#definitio.@value: In instances where a risk was notified to and accepted onto the register of a more Senior Manager for oversight it may be that following the implementation of actions the rating of the risk may have reduced to an acceptable or tolerable level or where remaining actions lie within the control of the Manager at the level below. In such circumstances a decision may be taken to ‘close’ the risk on the register and to de-escalate it onto the register of the Manager on the level below. Such risks when added to the register below are given a risk status of ‘open’ on that register and are reviewed at the next Management Team meeting of that Manager.

http://www.w3.org/2000/01/rdf-schema#com.@value: Process of comparing the results of risk analysis with risk criteria to determine whether the risk and/or its magnitude is acceptable or tolerable.

http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos#definitio.@value: Process of comparing the results of risk analysis with risk criteria to determine whether the risk and/or its magnitude is acceptable or tolerable.

http://www.w3.org/2000/01/rdf-schema#com.@value: A systematic process applied to the organisation’s objectives and activities to identify possible risk sources and causes and potential consequences or impacts should a risk occur.

http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos#definitio.@value: A systematic process applied to the organisation’s objectives and activities to identify possible risk sources and causes and potential consequences or impacts should a risk occur.

http://www.w3.org/2000/01/rdf-schema#com.@value: Coordinated activities to direct and control an organisation with regard to risk.

http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos#definitio.@value: Coordinated activities to direct and control an organisation with regard to risk.

http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos#definitio.@value: Tool for ranking and displaying risks by defining ranges for consequence and likelihood.

http://www.w3.org/2000/01/rdf-schema#com.@value: Communication and notification of risk from one level of the organisation to another.

http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos#definitio.@value: Communication and notification of risk from one level of the organisation to another.

http://www.w3.org/2000/01/rdf-schema#com.@value: A risk profile is a written description of a set of risks. A risk profile can include the risks that the entire organisation must manage or only those that a particular function or part of the organisation must address. (In the HSE, a services risk profile is set out in their risk register).

http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos#definitio.@value: A risk profile is a written description of a set of risks. A risk profile can include the risks that the entire organisation must manage or only those that a particular function or part of the organisation must address. (In the HSE, a services risk profile is set out in their risk register).

http://www.w3.org/2000/01/rdf-schema#com.@value: With the completion of some or all of the actions the level of risk (the rating) may be reassessed in order to consider whether its likelihood or impact score has reduced.

http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos#definitio.@value: With the completion of some or all of the actions the level of risk (the rating) may be reassessed in order to consider whether its likelihood or impact score has reduced.

http://www.w3.org/2000/01/rdf-schema#com.@value: A risk register is a database of assessed risks that face any organisation at any one time. Always changing to reflect the dynamic nature of risks and the organisation’s management of them, its purpose is to help managers prioritise available resources to minimise risk and target improvements to best effect.

http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos#definitio.@value: A risk register is a database of assessed risks that face any organisation at any one time. Always changing to reflect the dynamic nature of risks and the organisation’s management of them, its purpose is to help managers prioritise available resources to minimise risk and target improvements to best effect.

http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos#definitio.@value: Being alert to the potential of harm occurring within the workplace. The heightened sense of awareness that you need to adopt and engender within the workplace to ensure ongoing safety in the delivery of services.
